1.title: Cycle loss is not heating power
1.question: Which maximum survives when the measured quantity and intervention are stated precisely?
rivals: Drive amplitude or phase changes with frequency.
A mixture of relaxation times replaces the single-time closure.
falsifiers: A calibrated susceptibility spectrum fails the single-time relation beyond declared uncertainty.
Positive cycle loss fails the independent passive energy budget.
1.limitations: Synthetic fixed parameters; no material, apparatus or clinical endpoint was measured.

2.title: Thermometer lag distorts inferred power
2.question: Can one constant power produce different finite-window estimates solely through sensor lag and heat loss?
rivals: Absorbed power changes during the pulse.
Multiple thermal compartments or ambient drift invalidate the lumped model.
falsifiers: Independently calibrated parameters fail to predict a held-out heating duration.
2.limitations: The reference thermal model does not identify all absolute parameters without an external calibration.

3.title: One frequency can hide two particle populations
3.question: Does a one-frequency match survive held-out frequencies and controlled viscosity changes?
rivals: Instrument phase error creates apparent multiple relaxation times.
Aggregation or temperature drift changes the sample between viscosity conditions.
falsifiers: A calibrated held-out response disagrees with the fitted single-time or parallel-rate model beyond tolerance.
3.limitations: A successful fit need not uniquely identify the microscopic relaxation mechanism.

4.title: Response weights are not particle counts
4.question: Can size-dependent response weighting corrupt a population inferred from an average diameter or spectral weight?
rivals: The measured distribution is intensity-weighted rather than number-weighted.
Particle density, shape, magnetization or aggregation differs from the closure.
falsifiers: The number-weighted mass sum disagrees with the selected moment formula.
A wrongly weighted spectral model fails held-out frequencies despite matching a calibration point.
4.limitations: Declared spherical, equal-density and common-magnetization approximations; not a measured real suspension.

5.title: A beat depends on the measurement channel
5.question: What survives a linear channel, and what appears only when a detector squares the actual exported waveform?
rivals: A source tone or sideband already lies at the chosen rate.
Finite windows, fades, leakage, transducer nonlinearities or unequal RMS confound the comparison.
falsifiers: Actual WAV Fourier projections disagree with the frozen predicted components.
A declared linear channel creates a new component without an implemented nonlinear operation.
Equal-RMS or phase-reversal controls fail the claimed quadratic-detector prediction.
5.limitations: Digital amplitude and squared amplitude are not calibrated pressure, acoustic intensity, nanoparticle force or a clinical endpoint.
